chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, who said:

When Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had breakfast at my place, the basin was brought and was started with, and it was in the front of the gathering. He said, 'Begin with the one on your right.' When one had performed ablution, the boy wanted to lift the basin, so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, 'Leave it (and wash your hands in it).'

key_terms.الطَّاشْتِ: Basin or bowl used for holding water for ablution
key_terms.صَدْرِ الْمَجْلِسِ: The front or foremost part of the gathering

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of sharing water and performing ablution during a meal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Imam’s emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and communal sharing, specifically prioritizing the right-hand side as a sign of honor and ensuring the reuse of water for multiple participants. It highlights the practical application of modesty and resourcefulness in daily rituals, reinforcing the Shia tradition of observing subtle social graces even during simple meals.
